title: Rate of Change of Area of a Circle
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Let A(r) = pi*r^2 be the area of a circle with radius r. Find the average rate of change of area when r increases from 3 to 3.5, and compute the instantaneous rate of change of area with respect to radius at r = 3.

steps.title: Compute Average Rate of Change on [3, 3.5]
steps.explanation: Evaluate the area at r = 3 and r = 3.5 and divide the change in area by the radius change Delta r = 0.5.
steps.why: Average rate is the ratio of area increment to radius increment.

steps.title: Formulate the Instantaneous Rate of Change
steps.explanation: Express the instantaneous rate of change at arbitrary radius r as the limit of the difference quotient.
steps.why: Instantaneous rate of change is the derivative defined by the difference quotient limit.

steps.title: Expand and Cancel the Parameter h
steps.explanation: Expand the squared binomial, subtract the original area, and factor out h.
steps.why: Canceling h eliminates the indeterminate form and reveals the circumference formula.

steps.title: Evaluate at r = 3
steps.explanation: Substitute r = 3 into the derived rate formula 2*pi*r.
steps.why: The instantaneous rate of change of circular area with respect to radius equals its circumference.
